brief_extract: We now have six prospective individual Trustees for the continuation of the work of the CHMT into 1987 and beyond. NORAH RIDDINGTON

23 YEARS OF SERVICE IN THE WISE AND SAFE USE OF ELECTRICITY IN THE HOME

“Are you sure you are in the right room?” demanded one of the all-male group of committee members seated around the conference table when the young Norah Riddington, shortly after joining the EAW in 1963, attended her first BSI Technical Committee to discuss domestic electric appliances. Even now, some 23 years later, she can find herself the lone woman on some of the committees on which she serves.

“I have been very grateful for the example and influence of my three predecessors as Director”, Norah says. “Unfortunately I did not meet Dame Caroline but I heard a very great deal about her from my mother who was a member of the EAW and had been Chairman and President of the Southampton Branch.”

Within a year or so of joining the EAW, Norah found herself involved in a wide spread of activity on behalf of the Association. It was a time when the consumer interest was coming to the fore; when measuring performance of domestic appliances became fashionable; when safety became a major issue.
